Author: @paahtis6430
Content:
It's crazy how good nothing phones are for their price. All of them really. I know it's likely their strategy to just penetrate the market with lower prices to gain a desired market share, but only time will tell if they'll actually start increasing the prices. 

I've had the nothing phone 2 for a year now and I've honestly completely forgotten it's a nothing phone. Don't get me wrong, all the glyphs, the minimalistic icons and what not aren't unnoticeable. What I mean is, it's an every day tool, if it works, you don't even think about it. But if it doesn't work, even the smallest of annoyances will draw your attention on everyday use.

What I've been most surprised about is that I don't even have any protection on the glass and the phone still looks like new. I work on cars, camp, do farm work and what not. It has been dropped many times, it has got oil dripping over it and overall seen a lot. However borrowing a line from JerryRigEverything "glass is glass and glass breaks". It's only a matter of time (great now I have Linkin Parks Casualty as an earworm) till it breaks and I've probably been lucky so far.

Overall, I have nothing to complain about. No, I mean, Nothing has worked great. God..., Nothing works! Nothing is awesome. Buy Nothing. Nothing to add, thank you.

Author: @sujoymudli07
Content:
I really appreciate the recent software changes and new features introduced by Nothing. The Private Space feature, in particular, looks very modern and stylish.

I would like to request a feature addition: please consider bringing "Dash Share" to the Phone Manager app. It was available in earlier OnePlus devices like the OnePlus 7 and 7T, and it was extremely useful for many users.

I also loved the inclusion of a charger in the box and the colored SIM ejector pin — these small touches are really thoughtful.

However, I do have a few suggestions for improvement:

Please consider adding Gorilla Glass protection for better durability.

The screen bezels could be made thinner; in 2025, thicker bezels feel a bit outdated, and the bezel design in the Nothing Phone 3a still looks somewhat dated.

Given Carl Pei’s involvement, introducing a feature like the "Alert Slider" would be an excellent move. It’s a very practical feature that users would definitely appreciate on Nothing phones.


Thank you for continuing to innovate and listen to the community!

Author: @Lukas-rd4ul
Content: So CMF figured out all the little modularity of the first phone no one really used, so they scrapped the idea and focused on making a great budget phone. All the gimmicks are now hidden under the idea of using an extra cover/case for your lanyard etc., like any other case does. The main reason is the good price nobody is going to buy extra lenses that needs an extra case for their $200 budget camera phone. The idea of modularity just got ruled out, never to be seen again. Phone One was modular-ish, so people expected for Phone 2 interchangeable components — so you could cheap out on the camera but afford a better display, or swap the battery, in generell repairability — that’s modular. Now it’s all just an accessory. So forget the features: it’s a pretty good phone for a good price, and that’s really what it’s all about — but for that, it’s definitely recommendable.

The 20-million-dollar question is, what comes to mind when thinking of a modular phone? A removable, maybe hot-swappable battery. Not having this de facto USP has been a missed opportunity. Author: @ryanchong4372
Content:
I think the reason why they went with the irreplacable back for this CMF Phone 2 instead of continuing the design philosophy of the first is the same reason why that one modular phone designed by Google back in 2013 (Project Ara) became discontinued; the fact that you could replace certain parts in the phone instead of having to replace the whole thing meant that the some parts of the phone would be in higher demand than others; this would lead to part shortages or wastage, meaning most likely the Nothing company would either have to predict which parts would be in demand and not, or incur heavy losses from high wastage and complaints/customer service issues from inventory shortage of certain parts.

Of course, the higher customizability of the CMF Phone 1 was really intriguing and novel in comparison to how samey the rest of the other brand of phones has become, and I would've really loved it if they continued developing the phone with this idea in mind. However, as a business model its not really sustainable or reliable, and I can understand why they had to deviate from it. Wish they could've found a way to make this business model more feasible, its much more interesting than whatever we have today tbh.
